system: civil law system influenced by French legal tradition

constitution.amend: proposed by joint agreement of the chief of state (the prince) and the National Council; passage requires two-thirds majority vote of National Council members

courts.highest: Supreme Court (consists of 5 permanent members and 2 substitutes)
courts.judges: Supreme Court members appointed by the monarch upon the proposals of the National Council, State Council, Crown Council, Court of Appeal, and Trial Court
courts.lower: Court of Appeal; Civil Court of First Instance

citizenship.descent: the father must be a citizen of Monaco; in the case of a child born out of wedlock, the mother must be a citizen and father unknown

world: has not submitted an ICJ jurisdiction declaration; non-party state to the ICCt

executive.chosen: the monarchy is hereditary; minister of state appointed by the monarch from a list of three French national candidates presented by the French Government
executive.cabinet: Council of Government under the authority of the monarch

gov.divisions: no first-order administrative divisions as defined by the US government, but 4 quarters (quartiers, singular - quartier)

b: You could get a fine if you walk around in swimsuits, stripped to the waist, or barefoot, apart from on beaches and in bathing areas.
